content.text:
Both leads are resolved, and I found (and closed) a gap that would have mattered a lot: I checked whether the fix would actually defer Adyen's download, or just relocate it to a differently-named file the size-check doesn't look at.

**#3 — Adyen CDN loading: dead end, confirmed at the bundle level, not just the README.** `@adyen/adyen-web` does support `<script>`-tag loading per its own README — but that's *raw* Adyen Web. The package actually used here, `@adyen/adyen-salesforce-pwa` (the official Salesforce wrapper), doesn't just recommend npm — its **compiled bundle** contains a literal `require("@adyen/adyen-web")` and pulls 5 named exports off it (`AdyenCheckout`, `ApplePay`, `GooglePay`, `PayPal`, `Donation`). A CDN script only ever exposes a single global object, not that shape. Using CDN-loading here would mean throwing away the official Salesforce wrapper and rebuilding all of Adyen's SFCC/PWA Kit glue by hand — a rewrite, not a config change, to solve a bundle-size problem. Off the table.

**#1 — the real fix, and it's genuine, not cosmetic.** PWA Kit officially supports a root `webpack.config.js` that extends its default config — I verified the exact CLI code (`@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev@3.18.0`, confirmed installed version) that checks for this file on both `npm run build` and `npm start`, cross-checked against the original Salesforce PR that introduced it and the current official docs. Nothing here needs guessing.

The part I had to dig for myself: **does the fix actually defer Adyen, or just rename the file it hides in?** Checked where all three Adyen-importing files sit in the route tree — `Checkout`, `CheckoutRedirect`, and `CheckoutConfirmation` are **all** already lazy-loaded (`loadable(() => import(...))`) — two in this repo's own [routes.tsx](overrides/app/routes.tsx), the third (`Checkout` itself) in the base template's `routes.jsx`. Adyen is *only ever* reached through those three. So a new webpack cache-group that isolates `@adyen/*` into its own chunk will inherit that same "only loads if you're actually on checkout" behavior — homepage/PDP/PLP visitors stop downloading it entirely. This is a real fix, not a metric trick.

**The concrete change:** a root `webpack.config.js` (~10-15 lines) that requires PWA Kit's base config array and adds one new cache group — `@adyen/*` at higher priority than the existing catch-all `vendor` group. **Zero changes to any application file** — `payment.tsx`, `checkout-redirect`, `confirmation` stay exactly as they are, same imports, same behaviour.

**Two things worth flagging, not deciding on my own:**
1. That new file isn't listed in `frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md` today, but it controls code-splitting for every production bundle — by this repo's own precedent (the `request-processor.js` "add here when populated" pattern), it belongs with Integration/SI-Partner, not as an unowned file that happened to slip in.
2. `package.json`'s `bundlesize` array only ever checks `build/main.js` and `build/vendor.js` (confirmed) — after this fix, the new `adyen.js` chunk has no budget watching it at all. Worth adding a third entry while we're in there so it can't silently balloon again later.

content.text:
No decision made — here's the full walkthrough before you choose.

**What we're doing:** Adding one new file at the repo root, `webpack.config.js`. All it does is tell the build: "keep Adyen's code in its own separate file instead of dumping it into the one shared file every single page downloads." Nothing in the application code changes — `payment.tsx`, `checkout-redirect`, `confirmation` stay exactly as they are today.

**Why we're doing it:** The shared file (`vendor.js`) is over its size budget for exactly one reason — Adyen's code is stuck inside it. That "stuck" part is the actual bug: Adyen is only ever used on checkout, but the build's current rule says "every third-party package, no matter which page uses it, goes into this one shared file" — so it rides along with things like React that genuinely are needed on every page. We're not shrinking Adyen or removing functionality — we're just telling the build to stop merging something checkout-only into something that ships everywhere.

**What our basis is — i.e. what's actually been checked, not assumed:**
- The rule causing the merge is real and named: `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/config.js` lines 232-251, a `vendor` cache-group with a fixed output name and `chunks: 'all'`. I read this file directly.
- Proof the rule, not the import style, is the cause: two of the three files using Adyen already lazy-load it (`checkout-redirect`, `confirmation`), and Adyen still ends up in the shared file anyway. If eager-vs-lazy imports were the problem, those two would already be fine. They aren't.
- The fix mechanism (a root `webpack.config.js` overriding PWA Kit's default) isn't a workaround I invented — it's Salesforce's own documented extension point. I had a research agent trace the exact CLI code that checks for this file, then I independently re-ran those same greps myself and got identical line numbers back, and cross-checked it against the original Salesforce GitHub PR that added the feature plus their current developer docs.
- The CDN-loading alternative was ruled out at the same rigor, not on a hunch: I had a second agent check whether Adyen's SDK could be loaded via a script tag instead (avoiding the bundler entirely). It can — but only the raw SDK, not the official Salesforce wrapper package this codebase actually uses. I confirmed that myself by grepping the wrapper's actual compiled code, not just its README: it hard-`require()`s the npm package and pulls out 5 specific exports, a shape a CDN script's single global object can't provide. Using the CDN would mean deleting the official wrapper and hand-rewriting Adyen's SFCC integration — ruled out as disproportionate.
- The one thing I couldn't take on faith: whether the fix would actually delay Adyen's download, or just rename the file it hides in. So I checked where all three Adyen-importing files sit in the routing tree. All three — `Checkout`, `CheckoutRedirect`, `CheckoutConfirmation` — are already lazy-loaded (confirmed in this repo's `routes.tsx` for two of them, and in the base template's `routes.jsx` for the third). Nothing eagerly pulls Adyen in today. That means isolating it into its own chunk keeps that same "only loads if you're on checkout" behaviour — it doesn't just pass the test, it actually stops shipping Adyen to your homepage/PDP/PLP visitors.

**End result:** `vendor.js` drops back under its 550KB budget (Adyen was the entire cause of the overage — nothing else changed in that PR), `Deploy Dev` goes green again, and the 9 currently-open PRs stop inheriting a failure that has nothing to do with their own changes. Beyond CI: every page that isn't checkout genuinely stops downloading Adyen at all — a real mobile-performance win, not just a passing gate. Checkout itself keeps working identically, since no checkout code is touched. The only loose ends are the two governance/hygiene points I flagged: the new file isn't yet listed as anyone's responsibility in this repo's protected-file docs, and nothing currently watches the new Adyen-only chunk's size going forward.

So — implement it now on a new branch, flag the ownership question to whoever owns Tier-1 build config first, or something else?

Running `npm run build` locally runs a `build-translations` step first (extract-default-messages
→ compile-folder → compile-pseudo), which rewrites `translations/en-US.json`, `translations/en-GB.json`,
and every file under `overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/` — picking up any `defaultMessage`/`id`
react-intl strings added by recent merges that were never re-extracted and committed. This happens
on *every* local build, not just the first one.

**Why:** discovered while verifying an unrelated fix (the Adyen vendor.js bundle-size regression,
2026-09-14) — `npm run build` (called internally by `npm run test:max-file-size`) left 6 translation
files showing as modified in `git status`, despite the fix touching only `webpack.config.js` and
`package.json`. These files are Tier 2 ("Translations", Integration/SI-Partner-owned per
[[project-adyen-vendor-bundle-regression]]'s sibling protectedFiles.md) — committing them alongside
unrelated work would silently cross into someone else's ownership domain and bloat the diff with
noise that has nothing to do with the actual change.

**How to apply:** after any local `npm run build`, `npm start` equivalent, or `test:max-file-size`
run, check `git status` before staging anything. If translation files show as modified and the task
at hand isn't actually about translations, discard them (`git checkout -- translations/en-*.json
overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/*.json`) before committing — don't assume a clean-looking
diff just because you only *edited* two files yourself. This will keep happening on every future
local build in this repo; it is not a one-off fluke to investigate further.

`develop`'s `Deploy Dev` workflow (the continuous auto-deploy-on-push tier) has been failing
since [PR #71](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/71) (SFCC-662, Adyen install,
merged 2026-09-11): `vendor.js` is 878.64 KB gzip vs. a 550 KB budget, because
`@adyen/adyen-salesforce-pwa`/`@adyen/adyen-web` are imported eagerly (no code-splitting) in
three route files — `overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx:16` (a raw `require()`,
not even `import()`), `overrides/app/pages/checkout-redirect/index.tsx:3`,
`overrides/app/pages/confirmation/index.tsx:3` — so the whole SDK lands in the global chunk
shipped on every page, not just checkout. `main.js` itself is unaffected (132.92 KB, fine).

**Why:** `Deploy Dev`'s bundle-size job isn't a PR-time check — only `deploy-test.yml`/
`digital-sit.yml` gate on bundle size pre-merge. `Deploy Dev` runs post-merge, continuously, on
every push to `develop`, so PR #71 merged clean and only broke once landed.
[PR #108](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/108) (SFCC-132 badges, merged
2026-09-14, commit `ece4fc5`) landed on top of the still-broken base and is an innocent
bystander — Marcel flagged it as "the failed merge sitting in develop" but the badges PR itself
did nothing wrong; its own `main.js` delta is negligible.

**How to apply:** As of 2026-09-14, `dev` hasn't had a real deploy since PR #105 (2026-09-09) —
5 days / 2 merges stale — because `Deploy to dev` is skipped whenever `Dev Gate` fails. 6 open
PRs at the time of writing (#100, #106, #107, #109, #110, #111) will each re-trigger this same
failure on merge without fixing it — don't assume a fresh red `Deploy Dev` run is a new bug caused
by whatever just merged; check this first. Recommended fix (matches AGENTS.md's own performance
rule, "prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render"):
dynamic-import/lazy-load the Adyen SDK in those 3 files instead of eager top-level import —
touches only Tier 4 files, no Tier 1/2 approval needed, a normal `fix/*` branch off `develop`.
Marcel chose "just brief me, no code" on 2026-09-14 — **no fix branch was created this session,
the regression is still live.** Before relying on any of this in a future session, re-check
`gh run list --workflow deploy-dev.yml --branch develop --limit 5` and `gh pr list --state open`
— confirm it's still broken and still unclaimed rather than assuming this snapshot still holds.

---
name: adyen-vendor-bundle-regression
description: develop's Deploy Dev CI gate failed 2026-09-11 to 2026-09-14 (PR #71) — vendor.js exceeded its 550kB budget because Adyen landed in the shared vendor chunk; fixed via a webpack cache-group carve-out, verified locally on fix/adyen-vendor-chunk-split, not yet merged
metadata:
  type: project
---

`develop`'s `Deploy Dev` workflow (continuous auto-deploy-on-push tier) failed from
[PR #71](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/71) (SFCC-662, Adyen install, merged
2026-09-11) through [PR #108](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pull/108) (SFCC-132
badges, merged 2026-09-14, commit `ece4fc5` — an innocent bystander that just landed on the
already-broken base): `vendor.js` was 878.64 KB gzip vs. a 550 KB budget.

**Root cause, verified — not the first theory tried:** it is NOT eager vs. dynamic imports.
`@adyen/adyen-salesforce-pwa`/`@adyen/adyen-web` are used in exactly 3 files —
`overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx`, `overrides/app/pages/checkout-redirect/index.tsx`,
`overrides/app/pages/confirmation/index.tsx` — and all 3 are reached only through already-lazy
routes (`Checkout`/`CheckoutRedirect`/`CheckoutConfirmation`, confirmed via `loadable()` in both
this repo's `overrides/app/routes.tsx` and the base template's
`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx`). The real cause is
`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/config.js` lines 232-251: a `vendor`
cache-group with a **static** `name: 'vendor'` and `chunks: 'all'` that merges *every*
node_modules package — sync or async — into one physically-named file. Because that file also
carries genuinely-eager deps (React, Chakra), anything merged into it rides along as eager too,
regardless of how it's actually used.

**Why the first fix idea (dynamic `import()`) was wrong:** disprovable from the code alone — 2 of
the 3 files already lazy-load Adyen via their route, and it still ended up in `vendor.js` anyway.
Static vs. dynamic import was never the lever; the cache-group's static name was.

**CDN/script-tag loading was investigated and ruled out**, not assumed: `@adyen/adyen-web`
supports it, but `@adyen/adyen-salesforce-pwa` (the package actually used here) does not — its
compiled `dist/app/index.js` does a literal `require("@adyen/adyen-web")` and destructures 5 named
exports (`AdyenCheckout`, `ApplePay`, `GooglePay`, `PayPal`, `Donation`), a shape a CDN script's
single global can't provide without dropping the official wrapper and reimplementing Adyen's SFCC
glue by hand.

**The fix, implemented and verified locally on branch `fix/adyen-vendor-chunk-split`
(2026-09-14), not yet committed/pushed/PR'd:**
- New root `webpack.config.js` (plain `.js` — PWA Kit hard-requires this exact filename, checked
  in both `bin/pwa-kit-dev.js`'s build command and `ssr/server/build-dev-server.js`'s dev-server
  path). Requires the base config array (`@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/config`), finds
  the `client` entry by `.name === 'client'`, adds a new `adyen` cache group (`test` matching
  `node_modules/@adyen/`, `chunks: 'all'`, `priority: 10` — must outrank the default vendor
  group's implicit 0). Zero application-code changes.
- `package.json`'s `bundlesize` array gained a third entry, `build/adyen.js` at `400 kB` max
  (measured actual: 363.34 KB gzip) — this chunk had no budget watching it before.
- **Measured result:** `vendor.js` 878.64 KB → 515.21 KB gzip (under its 550 KB budget again);
  `adyen.js` 363.34 KB (new, under its 400 KB budget); `main.js` unaffected at 132.94 KB. Full
  `npm run test:max-file-size` (the exact CI command) passes: 3/3 checks. `npx tsc --noEmit`
